picks.headline: Amazon KDP limits authors to two titles per format per week
picks.excerpt: Amazon KDP now caps uploads at two titles per format per week (down from 10); Amazon began setting upload limits in fall 2023 due to the flood of generative-AI books.
picks.rationale: The most actionable item: a platform rule change (10 uploads a week cut to 2) that changes release planning for every self-published author right away. It is a direct response to the flood of AI-generated books.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the new cap and who it affects. Present AI-book volume as the stated background, as the source does. The og_image is Jane Friedman's generic premium banner, so ax-media should source a distinct image.

picks.headline: SCBWI updates its AI policy to prohibit use in the creative process
picks.excerpt: Their policy is a strong model but also one of the strictest I’ve seen, banning generative AI for brainstorming or an editing pass.
picks.rationale: A new, concrete policy from a major children's-publishing body. It bans generative AI even for brainstorming or an editing pass, which directly affects how its members write and illustrate. It was yesterday's first backfill and is still fresh.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: state what is now banned (brainstorming, editing passes) and who it covers. Keep it distinct from rank 1: this is a professional-body policy, not a platform limit. The generic banner applies here too, so ax-media should source a distinct image.

picks.headline: AI and Scholarly Reading: Foxes versus Hedgehogs
picks.excerpt: Some readers are foxes, and some are hedgehogs. What kind of reader is AI, and how will that impact both the practice of science and the business of journal publishing?
picks.rationale: A fresh analysis of AI as a reader: broad-skimming 'fox' versus deep 'hedgehog', and what that means for research practice and journal publishing. It has its own article image.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: explain the fox/hedgehog framing and the conclusion for publishers. This is an opinion essay, so attribute its claims to the author.

picks.headline: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Redrawing the Map
picks.excerpt: A more compact Frankfurt Book Fair sets aside extra space for AI, audiobooks and comics, with an unusually large cohort of AI-focused service providers and a Hall 4.1 Innovation Stage.
picks.rationale: The biggest rights fair has been reorganised with dedicated AI space, a large group of AI service providers and an Innovation Stage. It is a useful preview of the AI tools publishers will be pitched next month.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: focus on the AI footprint (the AI service-provider cohort, the Hall 4.1 Innovation Stage). The 'AI Narration Beyond the Lab' debate from PW's companion 'Must-see Events' piece can be mentioned as a detail; that piece was folded in here as a same-source, same-topic duplicate.

picks.headline: Guest Post — Peer Review Triage: Deciding What’s Worth Saving
picks.excerpt: Guest post argues the ubiquity of AI-assisted writing tools is inflating manuscript submissions and straining peer-review capacity, and asks what of the current system is worth saving.
picks.rationale: AI writing tools are driving up manuscript submissions and straining peer-review capacity. It is a different angle from rank 3 (the supply side of submissions versus how AI reads), and it is the best remaining item after the duplicates and soft pieces were dropped.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with the causal claim (AI-assisted writing inflating submissions) and the triage options proposed. This is a guest opinion piece, so attribute it.
